w_c_run_timing.rule: W-C holds its frame-109 arc until the onset and reaches the frame-116 top arc at t_top (Fritsch-Carlson run). Blurred frames 109, 111 and 114 are exposure constraints, not keyframes: the run starts within frame 109's exposure, and during the exposures of 111 and 114 the skates reach the re-read row intervals (inputs.json run_marks; exposure at most 40 ms). Feasible = goal-line crossing inside the mouth on the +y side (replay), puck clearing the goalie and W-C after separation; chosen = nearest the centroid of the feasible region, or, if none is feasible, the least violating timing (crossing inside the mouth, then largest goalie clearance) with conflict_with_replay = true.

limitations: CONFLICT: with W-C's observed rotation, rigid carry and separation at peak slot speed, no run timing inside the frame-109/111/114 exposure constraints makes the puck enter on the replay's +y side clear of the goalie; the saved timing is the least violating one and the shot phase passes through the static goalie mesh. The rule-based shot leaves at 7.0 deg; straight paths from the same point that clear the goalie and enter on +y need 11.2-15.2 deg. Candidate causes: the contact rule (rigid carry, separation direction), an unobserved W-C rotation during the carry (only a +90 deg offset, which no frame shows, reproduces the replay), the goalie's position, assumed rotation or AI-mold size, or a different slot layout on the recorded edition.
